  15 minutes, then you build




How ScorePlay works,
and how to build on it
Jonas Verest, Deployment Lead, ScorePlay
Spurs² Hackathon, UT Austin
Part 1 · What ScorePlay is
Who we are, one library, one pipeline.
                                                                                                          Part 1 What ScorePlay is
Who we are: the media platform
sports organisations run on
ScorePlay stores, tags and distributes every photo and video a sports organisation
produces: live, fresh from the match, and from the archive.

01                                  02                              03                         04
Ingest                              Index                           Produce                    Distribute
every route in: upload, FTP, live   AI tags players and sponsors;   clip and log moments, in   share with sponsors,
feeds, on-site storage, archives    everything searchable           the platform               broadcasters and partners,
                                                                                               each with its own rights window


For Sports. By Sports.

                                                                                                                      Part 1 What ScorePlay is
Every upload runs as a workflow
A graph of steps, run on Temporal. Each organisation can customise it, per source. Fixed this week.
  The default workflow
                                                                                               The image branch on the left, the video branch
         Trigger                      If / else file_type == "image"                           on the right, both merge at index_full. Every
                                                                                               step has a success output and an error output.
                            true                                                           false
                                        image                                                                        false
        check_hash
        → duplicate
                                                                   If / else file_type == "video"
                                                                                           true
        compress                      image                        transcode                               video
        → original, compressed, thumbnail                          → proxies, stream, thumbnail, sprites

        extract_metadata              image
                                                                   launch_transcript                       video
        → players, sponsors, tags, texts


        index_full                              detect_faces   image video            detect_text               image video
         image video audio other                → players                             → players, sponsors, tags, texts

                                                                                                                                           05
                                                                                                                         Part 1 What ScorePlay is
A workflow is built from steps
  The steps a workflow can use
Image                                                                  Video
check_hash               checks the file's hash for duplicates         transcode                 makes the proxies, the stream and the
                                                                                                 previews
compress                 makes the compressed and thumbnail files
                                                                       ai_reframing              makes a cropped version
extract_metadata         reads EXIF and XMP metadata into fields
                         and tags                                      launch_transcript         starts the transcript
detect_faces             identifies players from their faces           All media
detect_text              reads text in the frame: names, numbers,
                         boards                                        index_full                makes the media searchable
detect_logos             detects sponsor logos                         add_media_tags            adds set tags
                                                                       check_duplicate_name checks for a media with the same name

                                                                       http_call                 calls an outside service
Each organisation picks and orders its steps, per source. http_call plugs in an outside service, for example a club's
own enrichment.

Part 2 · How we structure media
Collection, media, version, file, tag, log.
                                                                                                                           Part 2 How we structure media
A collection holds media, a media
holds versions, a version holds files
                                          1 Collection API object Event, field event_id
                                          Premier League › Manchester United vs Tottenham Hotspur - Week 6 › Match. A media sits in
                                          exactly one collection.

                                            2 Media ID, type
                                            130000990, Manchester United vs Spurs | Full Match | 2026-27.mp4, video
130000990
                                            Fields on it: name, date, captured_time, description, tc_in, tc_out, players, tags
Manchester United vs Spurs | Full Match
| 2026-27.mp4                                3 Version MediaVersion                                       5 Tags and logs
                                             default. An edit saved back becomes a second version.        Tags hang off the media (the full match
                                                                                                          carries 11 player tags).
                                               4 Files                                                    Logs sit on the video's timeline:
                                               original 8.1 GB, 1080p proxy 5.7 GB, 720p proxy 2.6 GB.    timecoded moments with their own tags,
                                               Also a thumbnail, an HLS stream and sprite strips.         players and comment (none yet).


A collection holds media. A media holds versions, a version holds files. Tags describe a media. A log is a tagged moment on a video. Search reads
all of it; the app you build writes all of it back.
                                                                                                                                                     08
                                                                                                                               Part 2 How we structure media
A media carries its own facts:
description, captured time, date

                              Photo 130001124                                                  Full match 130000990
                              PC1_9993.JPG                                                     Manchester United vs Spurs | Full Match | 2026-27.mp4

description                   Sandro Tonali of Tottenham Hotspur battles in the air            empty
captured_time                 2026:10:10 19:02:15                                              empty
date                          17 Oct 2026                                                      17 Oct 2026
size                          4204x2803                                                        video: 1920x1080, 25 fps, 6,334 s


date is the library date (here, the day the content was loaded). description is searchable. Also on a media: tc_in, tc_out
(next slide), players, tags.

On ingest, ScorePlay tags players
and sponsors from the frame

                                 Players              faces, matched to the players' headshots;                 a player tag

                                 Sponsors             logos; text on boards, shirts, backdrops                  a sponsor tag

                                 On your platform: 322 of 418 photos and 37 of 58 videos carry a player tag. No media carries a

                                                                                                              Part 2 How we structure media
A tag says who is in it, not when: logs are the moments
                                          Tags on the whole media: 11 players.
                                                                                    Logs: 0.
                                          0s                                                                                       6,334 s

130000990
Manchester United vs Spurs | Full Match
| 2026-27.mp4                               GET /media/130000990/logs
                                            {"items": [], "page": 1, "limit": 50}


                                            Tags describe the whole media. ScorePlay adds them on ingest.
                                            Logs are timecoded moments: a start, an end, tags, players, a comment. None are created by
                                            default: the app you build writes them.

Eight calls, in the order of the build loop.
                                                                                                     Part 3 The API, and how to use it this week
One header, one base URL: your first call is /whoami
                                                                                        Your key: create it in the platform under
   curl https://media.scoreplay.io/v1/whoami \                                          Settings › API key. A team admin key has 175
      -H "X-ScorePlay-Api-Key: $KEY"                                                     rights .


   {"user_id": 85146, "user_type": "admin",
                                                                                        A missing right returns 401 , the same as a
    "company": {"name": "spurs2-hack-10", ...},
                                                                                        bad key.
    "rights": ["can_do_media_download", ...], "scope": {...}}                           company_id       (5167 here) is needed to write
                                                                                        logs. It is not in /whoami : read it off any media.




Your IDs will differ from the ones on these slides. Same content, different platform.

                                                                                                                                             16
                                                                                                Part 3 The API, and how to use it this week
Find: from a name to its media in a few calls
  GET /tag/search?query=solanke
  → {"players": [{"ID": 728708, "full_name": "Dominic Ayodele Solanke-Mitchell", ...}],
      "tags": [], "sponsors": []}
  POST /event/search {"sub_and_master": true}            → the collections, as a bare array
  POST /media/search {"players": [728708], "media_type": "video"}                → count 15
  POST /media/search {"players": [728708], "media_type": "photo"}                → count 53




Filters you will use: players , tag_options , event_id , event_ids , media_type , transcript_query . Add any_ for OR, not_
to exclude.

                                                                                    Part 3 The API, and how to use it this week
Search fails quietly: four traps
  Four traps
Trap                               What you see                               Do this
event_id is not recursive          Match returns 399 media; with its 3 sub-   send event_ids with every ID
                                   collections 445; the match root 0

An unknown filter key is ignored   type: "photo" returns all 476;             test each filter with a fake ID: it must
                                   media_type: "photo" returns 418            return 0

tag_options means AND              a stale ID returns 0 results, no error     check your IDs before you search

Tag search matches substrings      son returns Robertson, Maddison,           pick by ID
                                   Richarlison...

                                                                                         Part 3 The API, and how to use it this week
Fetch the proxy, and keep the work on your machine
  Three names for the same files
Where                                        Names
media.files[].details                        photographer_quality, compressed_quality, thumbnail_quality

media.video.* (video only)                   proxy_large, proxy_medium, stream (HLS), thumbnail, sprite_small,
                                             sprite_full

GET /media/{id}/formats/download             original, video_large, video_medium (photo: original, compressed)



  GET /media/130000990/formats/download        → pick video_medium (720p) or video_large (1080p)
  GET <file_url>                               → the proxy; the URL lasts 24 hours




No editing and no compute from ScorePlay for the Hackathon.
Cut, crop and transcode on your own machine (ffmpeg, handout).

                                                                                                     Part 3 The API, and how to use it this week
Twelve Labs finds the moment, ScorePlay keeps it
  ScorePlay                                             your app             Twelve Labs
  the media library                                                          video understanding

Twelve Labs                         What it gives you
Marengo (search)                    a query in words or an image returns clips: video_id, rank, start, end in seconds
Pegasus (analyze)                   text from a video: summaries, answers, JSON to a schema you define




 a Marengo clip start, end (seconds)                                          a ScorePlay log start_offset, end_offset (seconds)
Both in seconds from the start of the video.
                                                                                                                                             20
                                                                                                              Part 3 The API, and how to use it this week
The main edit, on your machine: cut, stitch, 9:16, overlay
# 1 cut a moment from the proxy, frame-accurate
ffmpeg -ss 00:12:31 -to 00:12:46 -i proxy.mp4 -c:v libx264 -c:a aac a.mp4
# 2 stitch clips: list.txt holds        file 'a.mp4'     then   file 'b.mp4'
ffmpeg -f concat -safe 0 -i list.txt -c copy reel.mp4
# 3 reframe to 9:16, 1080x1920
ffmpeg -i reel.mp4 -vf "crop=ih*9/16:ih,scale=1080:1920" -c:a copy reel_9x16.mp4
# 4 overlay a logo, top right (a transparent PNG keeps its transparency)
ffmpeg -i reel_9x16.mp4 -i logo.png -filter_complex "[1]scale=300:-1[l];[0][l]overlay=W-w-40:40" -c:a copy final.mp4




 ffmpeg is open source and runs on your laptop: github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg.
 Then: upload final.mp4 into your sub-collection (slide 24) and log on the source what you used (slide 23).

 POST /event   {"name": "AI Shorts 9:16", "parent_id": 1469761,
                "external_id": "team10-ai-shorts", "tag_options": [{"id": ...}]}

                                                                                                                                23
                                                                                                Part 3 The API, and how to use it this week
Put content back in three steps
   POST /upload/event/{collection_id}?parts=1            {"name": "clip_9x16.mp4"}
     → {"upload_id": ..., "key": ..., "urls": [{"url": ...}], "media_id": ...}
   PUT <url>     (the file bytes)       → keep the ETag response header
   POST /upload/complete/{media_id}
     {"key": ..., "upload_id": ..., "parts_number": 1, "parts": [{"parts_number": 1, "etag": ...}]}




Then status:     WAITING    ›   PROCESSING      ›   TRANSFORMED     ›   DONE


About 40 seconds for an 8 second video. The upload then runs through the workflow of slide 5.

The loop, the two challenges, and where to get help
 1 Find                           2 Fetch                         3 Analyse                                4 Write back
 tag search, then media           the proxy.                      on Twelve Labs.                          tags, logs, uploads.
                                                                                                                                               5 Act.
 search.

                                                                       and round again

Assisted Auto-Production                                                            Rights and Compliance
one match in, what comes out, and for whom?                                         what can be published, where, and how do you show why?




Help: ScorePlay and Twelve Labs engineers are on the floor both days. Agree your taxonomy with us before writing. Docs: developer.scoreplay.io (Try-it console,
OpenAPI, Postman).

Your toolkit: what to install, where to read
Install          Command
ffmpeg           macOS brew install ffmpeg, Ubuntu sudo apt install ffmpeg, Windows winget install
                 Gyan.FFmpeg

ScorePlay        no SDK needed: any HTTP client, one header



Read             Where
ScorePlay API    developer.scoreplay.io (Try-it console, OpenAPI, Postman)
Twelve Labs      docs.twelvelabs.io: Search, Analyze, Metadata
ffmpeg           source: github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg · docs: ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg.html · stitching:
                 trac.ffmpeg.org/wiki/Concatenate
